description:
pkix-ct/src/verify.rs:671 — the comparison `if r != *expected_root` uses [u8;32] PartialEq, which short-circuits on first byte mismatch (variable-time). For SCT verification, this is not a problem: the SCT-verification flow is offline / does not run against attacker-controlled timing channels.

However the workspace ships SctVerifier for use inside chain validation pipelines that DO sometimes run against attacker-controlled timing (e.g., TLS handshake verification, web-side OCSP+SCT validation). A Merkle root mismatch leaks a few bytes of timing info about which byte of the reconstructed root first differs from the expected root — this is reconstructed from caller-controlled audit_path data, so an attacker who can choose audit_path can probe the expected root one byte at a time.

In practice this is a weak side channel (root_hash is public anyway, distributed via signed STH) and would require many billions of audit_path probes to recover. So P4 — flag, do not block.

Pre-1.0 it is free to use subtle::ConstantTimeEq::ct_eq() — matches what other crypto crates in the workspace do.

Suggested fix: import subtle::ConstantTimeEq, replace the != with ct_eq. Zero engineering cost; defense in depth.
title: Verify_sth uses constant-time eq via != on signature path but root_hash comparison in verify_inclusion_inner is non-CT
